title: Review: You Can See Everything blurs the view of Elizabeth Holmes' deceit
gist: Ars reviewer pans the A24 film You Can See Everything about Elizabeth Holmes's last days before prison as shallow and evasive about her deceit, arguing facts and accountability matter. Little investable content beyond Theranos fraud context.

insights.claim: The reviewer argues the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim film yields little fresh insight into Holmes and treats her with kid gloves while portraying partner Billy Evans harshly.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Critical reception is divided; awards-season buzz is expected regardless.

insights.claim: The review contends the film's pursuit of ambiguity and 'unknowable' truth obscures that Holmes's fraud is knowable, and that accountability matters in a post-truth media environment.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Narratives rehabilitating founders after fraud convictions face pushback.
insights.locator: The cynical nihilism of it all

insights.claim: Reviewer says the film is marketed as a documentary but works as an absurdist reality show, more for Nathan Fielder fans than for people interested in Theranos.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Genre mislabeling can affect audience expectations and reception.

insights.claim: Theranos was valued at $9 billion at its peak, and Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Reference case for founder fraud in venture-backed startups.

insights.claim: Whistleblower Tyler Shultz says the Theranos device shown in the film was a never-completed future product, not the device used to give patients inaccurate results.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates how misdirection was used to shape narratives.

insights.claim: Holmes and Evans moved from a $125 million estate into an average-looking rented condo for filming, a tactic used previously with journalists.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette

insights.claim: Evans is already raising capital for a new biomedical startup, and Holmes will be eligible for a halfway house next year.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Diligence on any Evans-linked biotech fundraising warrants extra care.
insights.locator: In the grand scheme of things
